findings.title: Data race on outer err variable in search.init goroutines
findings.body: In search.init, the goroutine passed to group.Go captures the outer 'err' variable that was declared at line 181 (stats, err := s.storage.GetResourceStats(...)). Because group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers) permits multiple goroutines to run concurrently, each goroutine writes to that outer 'err' at line 190 (err = s.build(...)) and reads it at line 191 (return err). Multiple goroutines writing to and reading from the same variable without synchronization is a data race that Go's race detector would flag. With the PR moving init to run unconditionally at startup with real concurrency (initWorkers > 1), the race is now reachable in normal operation. Declare a local err inside the closure (or return the build error directly) instead of reusing the outer variable.

findings.title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed counter
findings.body: totalBatchesIndexed is declared at line 177 and incremented (line 189: totalBatchesIndexed++) from inside the goroutine launched by group.Go. With group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers), multiple goroutines run in parallel and each performs a read-modify-write on the same counter without synchronization. The value reported in span.AddEvent at line 199 (and emitted via s.log.Info at line 216) is therefore non-deterministic. Use atomic.AddInt or a mutex around the increment.

findings.title: Unsynchronized writes to s.initErr in Stop can race with Init
findings.body: Stop (lines 320-342) writes to s.initErr (lines 321, 328, 339) without any synchronization, while Init (lines 293-318) both reads and writes s.initErr inside sync.Once. Since Init is part of the public ResourceServer interface and can be invoked by callers, a caller that calls Init and Stop concurrently will trigger a data race on s.initErr. The pre-existing lazy-init model made this easier to hit (any RPC handler could race with shutdown). Even though NewResourceServer now calls Init synchronously, the public surface still permits external concurrent use. Protect s.initErr with a mutex, or use atomic.Value/atomic.Pointer.

findings.title: Cancel function leaks if Init fails inside NewResourceServer
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancellable background context at lines 229-235 and stores its cancel function in s.cancel. It then calls s.Init(ctx) at line 258. If Init returns an error, NewResourceServer returns nil and the error at line 261, dropping the local s. The cancel function is never invoked, so the watcher context (and the goroutines that depend on it, including the event-pump goroutine spawned in search.init at line 207 and the broadcaster goroutine in initWatcher) cannot be cancelled by the caller. Any partial init work continues to consume backend resources (a SQL poller, an indexing goroutine) until the backend is independently stopped. Call cancel() before returning nil in the error path so the caller can recover cleanly and the background goroutines terminate.

findings.title: Postgres skip added instead of fixing the underlying test
findings.body: The PR adds an unconditional skip for postgres (lines 36-38) along with a TODO acknowledging the test should be fixed. The integration test now runs only when GRAFANA_TEST_DB is mysql (sqlite3 is also skipped). The most common CI database (postgres) is no longer covered by TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer, reducing confidence that the storage server target still works end-to-end. The TODO should be resolved rather than carrying the skip forward.
